title: restore first-boot path ignores the generation: an existing state object whose fetch error looks absent starts the bot empty
detail: entrypoint.sh:249 reads the generation (sg0); :265-267 returns 0 (first boot) whenever the fetch of both archives is absent by is_absent (:82, loose match on 404 / not found), without checking sg0 != 0. If the object exists but the cp error text matches, the bot starts with empty state; later snapshots are refused by the generation precondition, so nothing is overwritten. Breaks no criterion (B4-C1(b) is the object-absent case). Not reproduced; read from code.
fix_direction: in the first-boot branch treat sg0 != 0 as a read failure (return 1) instead of first boot.
class: file-dont-fix until the next unit touching entrypoint.sh

title: supervisor signal races: wait on an already-reaped child gives 127; a SIGTERM between the loop test and start_child is not forwarded to that tick
detail: entrypoint.sh:393-402 wait_child: if the signal lands after wait reaped the child, SIGS differs, the loop waits again on the reaped pid and CHILD_RC becomes 127 (measured: sh wait on a reaped pid returns 127). Attendance loop (:605-): a SIGTERM after the STOPPING test and before CHILD is set finds CHILD empty in on_term, so the new tick is never signalled (it runs until it ends or the container is killed, losing the final snapshot). Windows are milliseconds; not reproduced; the B4-C5 and I3 tests send SIGTERM mid-run and pass.
fix_direction: in wait_child keep the first non-127 status; in the loop re-check STOPPING after start_child and signal the child if set.
class: file-dont-fix until the next unit touching entrypoint.sh

title: record-once exits 0 when the record command succeeded but no recording exists
detail: entrypoint.sh:322-345 copy_recordings returns 0 with no record dir, no .webm or only 0-byte files; REC_RC stays 0 (the test for nothing recorded asserts exit 0 on purpose). B4-C6 as written (exit with the record command's status; skip zero-byte files) allows it. Product question: should a successful record with no recording be non-zero for the job runner.
fix_direction: owner decision; if wanted, exit 74 when nothing was copied and the record command reported success.

title: tar_contained splits name -> target at the first arrow: a symlink whose own name contains the arrow with an absolute target passes the validator
detail: Probe: crafted ustar with such a symlink gives tar_contained rc 0. GNU tar 1.35 then refuses to write through the symlink (Not a directory), so no write outside the trees occurred; defence in depth only. Related low: a killed periodic upload can leave a stale state.gen (final snapshot refused 412, fails safe); recordings of a SIGTERM-interrupted tick are not copied.
fix_direction: parse the link target from the tar -tzvf long listing by field, or reject names containing the arrow.
